findings.summary: The synthesizer corpus sends terminal_marker as a STRING (renderReportBody(marker) => "<!-- dr-terminal ... -->\n"), but dr-synthesizer's declared input contract agent-runtime profiles/roles/schemas/synthesizer-input.v1.json:28-36 declares terminal_marker as {"type":"object"} with stop/blocked/capHit. This same corpus object is what writeGenerateInputFile serializes into --input (src/generate.ts:243-247), and agent-runtime's validateJsonSchema recurses into every declared property present in the payload (dispatch.ts:448-457) emitting "expected object, got string" for a string, then fails the run with CONTRACT_ERROR at dispatch.ts:922-928. Every synthesizer dispatch therefore dies at the --input guard before the model runs, so the report leg of the wiring this package exists to establish cannot produce anything. Spec §2.2 line 81 names buildReportMarker() (which returns exactly {stop, blocked, capHit}) as the producer, not the renderer; the fix is engine-side and needs no agent-runtime change.

No test validates the engine-assembled corpus against agent-runtime's declared role input schemas, which is why the terminal_marker type violation ships undetected. The suite already reads agent-runtime profiles for D3 (agentRoleRoute / routes.yaml), so asserting each corpus against roles/schemas/debater-input.v1.json and roles/schemas/synthesizer-input.v1.json is directly feasible; D1 only asserts that evidence text appears in the positional argument and never checks that the --input payload it writes alongside actually satisfies the guard spec §1.1 assigns to --input.

GenerateSpawnRuntime.spawnProcess is optional and spawnGenerateRole guards it with `if (runtime.spawnProcess)`, so a runtime without it builds the argv, silently discards it, and still returns `{ body: await readBody(runId) }` for a run that was never launched. That is a silent zero-spawn fake success, the opposite of the loud-failure discipline the same repo enforces for worker dispatch (resolveAgentRunBin throws AgentRunUnresolvedError rather than fall back, and spawnAgentRunWorker calls spawnWorkerProcess unconditionally at src/tick-run.ts:736-741). No src code supplies a real process launcher for generation roles, so the terminal effect remains an injection seam with a no-op default.

writeGenerateInputFile writes a payload file into tmpdir() and nothing ever removes it, so every generation role leaks one temp file per dispatch. The comparable worker path deliberately binds payload lifetime to child exit and unlinks it (src/tick-run.ts:731-741), citing exactly this concern.

The D3 cases resolve agent-runtime through a hardcoded absolute host path (/data/code/self/agent-runtime/profiles) and throw on a missing file, so the whole suite turns red on any machine or CI runner without that path unless AGENT_RUNTIME_PROFILES is set. Every other test in the repo derives paths from a repo-relative ROOT; the D7 claim of 17 files / 317 tests green is therefore environment-conditional.
